## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater green alga in the family Scenedesmaceae, characterized by small colonies typically composed of four crescent- to kidney-shaped cells embedded in a thin gelatinous matrix. In a typical colony, two cells lie in roughly the same plane while the other two are oriented more vertically, producing an irregular three-dimensional arrangement. Each cell contains a parietal chloroplast with a pyrenoid. Tetrallantos lagerheimii occurs as part of the plankton in ponds, lakes, rivers, canals, and other freshwater habitats and has been recorded from both nutrient-poor and eutrophic waters. Like other planktonic green algae, it contributes to primary production and supports freshwater microbial food webs.
